# Community IPTV Player (CTV)

> A free, open source IPTV player that runs in the browser. Import any M3U playlist and stream
> live TV, movies, series and catch-up — no account, no ads, and nothing stored on a server.

Community IPTV Player is hosted at https://ctv.1guy.dev. It is a frontend-only application:
playlists, favourites, recents, watch progress and settings are all persisted in the browser's
local storage, and the app can export or import that state as JSON. There is no sign-up, no paid
tier and no advertising.

The project is also a deliberate argument that AI-written software can be released as free and
open source and still compete with paid players. It is MIT licensed and open to reuse.

This file exists because the interface is client-rendered: a fetcher that does not execute
JavaScript sees an empty document, so the description below is the readable version.

## Capabilities

- Import M3U playlists from a URL, pasted text, or a local file, and manage several of them.
- Browse live TV, movies, series and catch-up content.
- Playback with HLS support and native fallback, picture-in-picture, fullscreen and standard
  transport controls.
- Favourites, recents, continue-watching progress and per-playlist settings, all stored locally.
- Export and import the full application state as JSON.
- Installable as a PWA, and packaged as desktop apps for macOS and Windows.

## Notes for automated clients

- `/api/stream` is a server-side relay that proxies upstream media so the browser is not subject
  to the provider's CORS rules. It is a byte pipe for media, not an API worth crawling, and
  /robots.txt disallows `/api/`.
- The player ships no channel list or playlist of its own. Users supply their own sources.
